result.changelog:
All 7 entries kept (each 341-399 words); meta-language removed; game titles at most twice per entry.

Overview:
- Serialization now 'between 2002 and 2004', with no months.
- E-manga host is no longer named.
- Added two conflict notes: the Police/Army pre-hunter service (later account takes precedence) and the Raven Beak Mawkin DNA from Dread.
- Metroids now 'designed on Zebes, released on SR388'.
- Comic BomBom adaptation now named Metroid Prime: Episode of Aether.
- Unverified 'no official English release' line dropped.
- Keys: removed backstory, origin story and bare 'manga'; added Metroid manga, Magazine Z manga, Samus manga.

K-2L:
- Kept 'Chief Aran', Ridley's 'cute' line and the distress call: all three are confirmed on Metroid Wiki, despite the report.
- Dropped the 'refusal to let children die' clause.
- Keys: removed 'welding laser'; added Old Bird, Samus's parents, Aran family.

Upbringing:
- 'Per the manga, Gray Voice's DNA' plus the Dread/Raven Beak Mawkin DNA clause.
- SR388 named in place of 'unnamed frontier world'.
- 'First sample was later unveiled' without 'while Samus still lived there'.
- Fixed the 'computer interface' grammar.
- Kept 'Protectors of the Galaxy' and 'You can't be second or third place': Metroid Wiki gives both as exact manga text.
- Dropped the unsourced reproduction and motive claims.
- Keys: dropped the Chozo DNA/blood/genes keys; added Old Bird, Mother Brain's creation, Samus's childhood.

Federation Police:
- Replaced the invented Army-after-Police chronology with the Other M conflict note.
- One battleship, not a fleet.
- Both arrest quotes used in their correct places: Pg 17 'I'm with the Federation Police...' (the report wrongly called it a misquote) and Pg 29 'In the name of the Federation Police...'.
- Dropped the labor motive.
- Kept 'main forces moved on' (confirmed in Samus's Pg 12 line).
- Keys: dropped Hardy, height sensor, police squad, problem children.

Kreatz and Mauk:
- Dropped the 'only team of equals' claim and the cadets anecdote.
- 'Defeated' in place of 'taken'.
- Skree warning separated from the Pyonchi hand-off.
- Kreatz quotes kept: confirmed on Metroid Wiki.
- Mauk softened to 'quieter, more timid', per the Pyonchi page.
- Keys: only the four name keys.

Betrayal:
- Quote fixed to 'they are under our control'.
- Removed Old Bird's survival, the breeding ground and the 'coldness in every meeting' line.
- Escaped Chozo 'later disappeared'.
- Gray Voice's final attack follows the Gray Voice page and Japanese Wikipedia.
- 'Chozo Power Suit' in place of 'Chozo Battle Suit'.
- Keys: 'Mother Brain' and the secondary keys removed; Gray Voice, Platinum Chest, defective product and fall of Zebes now fire on their own.

Ridley trauma:
- Other M Ridley is now a clone, distracted by Anthony Higgs.
- 'Defeated' in place of 'taken'.
- 'Tourian' kept: it is in Metroid Wiki's manga summary.
- Invented inner states cut; 'For roleplay' rephrased.
- Keys: emotional words are primary and now need a secondary hit (Ridley, K-2L, Gray Voice, Kreatz, Mauk, Bottle Ship, Little Birdie); 'froze', 'breakdown', 'repressed' and 'nemesis' removed.
result.unresolved:
- Exact serialization months are unresolved (English Wikipedia and MyAnimeList disagree).
- Whether an official English release ever existed is unresolved (Metroid Wiki claims one in 2009), so the line was left out.
- 'Episode of Aether' rests on search snippets only; English Wikipedia cites the Japanese title as 'Metroid Prime'.
- The cause of Samus's dispute with Adam (the Ian claim) was not found in the sources read, so Ian is not named.
- Japanese Wikipedia says Samus was taken prisoner on Zebes; per the report the entries say only 'defeated'.
- Kreatz and Mauk's 'rescue' and the Chozo evacuation rest on Japanese Wikipedia alone.
- Old Bird's fate after the fall of Zebes is not recorded.
- 'Old Bird' is a key on two entries (K-2L and upbringing), so both fire together when he is mentioned.
